So the measure of a violation is not the welfare it costs but the possibility it forecloses against the will the subject could form. A benevolent dominator who provides for a subject in every material respect while enclosing what that subject may become commits the paradigm wrong: welfare left intact does not redeem a possibility-field seized. Domination is therefore not exhausted by inflicted suffering or direct command. It consists in acquiring unanswerable control over the possibilities another subject may realistically pursue. This carries the chapter's name forward into the politics — the wrong at the individual scale and the maximand at the political scale (§9, *maximum possibility*) are one currency, and foreclosing a subject's possibility against its formable will is what, scaled across a shared field, the political order exists to prevent. Measuring against the will the subject *could* form, rather than the will it happens to hold, also disarms the contented-captive objection: an enclosure that reaches into the will itself and quiets all protest is the most complete violation, not the absence of one.

This fixes the one limit consent cannot cross, and fixes it structurally rather than by hand. Consent can license almost anything — binding commitments, vows, lifelong arrangements — because a commitment is an exercise of the capacity to author one's possibility, not a surrender of it. What consent cannot reach is the arrangement whose content is the *effective* destruction of that capacity: to consent away the standing power to revise and exit one's commitments is to use present authorship to extinguish the feature that licenses authorship at all — the egoist's groundless self-exemption turned inward. Inalienability is therefore not an added axiom but the consent constraint applied to its own precondition.

The deeper reason is temporal. Consent reaches into the future — it authorizes what is going to happen, pinned to a particular arrangement of time, place, and act — but it reaches forward as a *standing* authorization, the live approval of the subject whose act it is, not a token transferred out of them. What licenses an act at the moment it occurs is therefore that it is still authorized at that moment; a past consent cannot govern a present act any more than yesterday's appetite can be eaten today. So consent carries forward as a default that holds unless withdrawn, never as a lock immune to its own withdrawal — and an arrangement purporting to bind a subject after their consent had lapsed would not be their authorization governing the act at all, but their earlier self overriding their present one. Revocability is not a permission added on top of consent; it is what consent, being the live state of the one whose act it is, already is.

Inalienability turns on effective foreclosure, not formal: a commitment merely costly to leave remains revisable, but one engineered toward inescapability — debt bondage, a ruinous exit penalty — destroys revisability as surely as a chain. And because commitments are often joint, the protected core is unilateral *exit*, not unilateral *amendment*: each subject always retains departure, while none may force a shared arrangement to reshape around them or conscript another into it. Exit preserves the door, not freedom from what was set in motion behind it — the responsibility an agent bears for its contribution to causal history ([§9.12](maximum-possibility.html#sec-9-12)) survives the departure.

Two distinct relations are doing the work here, and keeping them apart dissolves what would otherwise look like a single tangled obligation. Consent governs what may be *done to* a subject going forward — its body, its presence, its participation — and that authorization is the live, revocable state just described. Responsibility governs what a subject *owes for what it has already set in motion* — the contribution to causal history that [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) locates — and that is backward-looking, so withdrawing consent ends the authorization without erasing the responsibility. The two divide along a structural seam: consent attaches to the inalienable latitude a subject has over its own person; responsibility attaches to the external, substitutable performances a subject's choices produce in the shared world. What sorts a case is whether the thing relied upon can be made good by substitution without reaching the promisor's body. Where it can — goods, payment, the product of labor — withdrawal is permitted but carries *reparative* responsibility for the reliance it induced: bounded by what repair requires, tracking the withdrawing subject's actual contribution to the other's loss, never a penalty added to make leaving irrational. Where it cannot — where the only thing that would satisfy the reliance is the subject's own body or intimate participation — no reliance interest can attach at all, because to price the withdrawal would be to price the body, the standing seizure of latitude the framework names as its limit case ([§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12)); and a conviction does not dissolve it, the point [§9.12](maximum-possibility.html#sec-9-12) carries into the carceral case. A bodily commitment is therefore never specifically enforceable and never carries a withdrawal penalty; what was exchanged for it, if anything, settles on the external track as a return, while the body itself stays beyond the reach of the debt. This is why a personal-service promise yields damages but never compelled performance, and why one may always leave an intimate arrangement at no charge to the leaving while remaining answerable for the external entanglements — shared property, created dependents — the arrangement produced.

One loss this leaves deliberately unrepaired: where what the other wanted was itself the freely-given participation now withdrawn, no substitution can restore it, and the framework declines to try, since the only available remedy would be to commodify the inalienable. That loss is borne, not transferred; bearing it is the price of keeping the body beyond purchase, and the account marks it as a cost it accepts rather than a gap it has closed.

The procedure is the structural account in operational form, not a metaphysical addition to it. Its terms — *consent*, *authorization*, *third party*, *capacity* — are the standard vocabulary moral and political philosophy already use. What the structural account adds is grounding: consent is the operational form of autonomy because subjects have privileged access to their own conditions that no external observer can match; Mill's harm principle follows because freedom and the limits on it both rest on the metaphysics of distinct subjects in shared exchange; justice extends to the field because subjects exchange inside conditions that either sustain or starve continued participation. The vocabulary was right. The grounding is what was missing.

Morality read as constitutive relation among mutually exposed subjects in a necessarily instantiated medium converges with what every serious meta-ethical position was tracking: Platonist robustness without the Platonic property, divine-command weight without the external lawgiver, Mackie's queerness diagnosis without the eliminative conclusion, Parfit's *reductio* deflected because the structural account does not deny mattering, Railton's idealization grounded one step down, Boyd's homeostatic cluster located in the conditions that hold it, Wielenberg's *sui generis* result returned to the natural order, Korsgaard's constructed normativity floored in what the constructor does not invent, Scanlon's reasonableness grounded in the structure reasonableness was already responding to, Blackburn's quasi-realism earned by structural necessity rather than projection, the neo-sentimentalist's fittingness explained by what the sentiments track. The four duties — non-maleficence, beneficence, autonomy, justice — are aspects of one move at the operational layer: act on the other subject's own readings rather than on your projection of them. The register in which subjects carry to each other what propositions cannot is taken up at [§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13).

## 8.13 Art {#sec-8-13}

Where language is built to carry a claim, art is built to carry a *feel*, how something shows up to a particular mind: how death, or a face, or a city, or autumn looks and weighs from where one person stands. It does this not by stating it but by making something another person can take in: a poem, a song, a painting, a film. What art carries is exactly the part that survives paraphrase: you can summarize a poem's point, but the summary is not the poem. And the receiver does not get a photocopy of the maker's experience; the made thing sets off a reading of their own, which is why a single work keeps yielding new responses across different people and across centuries. Beauty is the name for what happens when a mind and some structure in the world resonate, and art is the practice of making that resonance shareable.

::: {.identification}
**Art** · *Identification*

Art is the making of a vehicle that carries *how* some structure shows up to a particular mind (a perspectival reading) across the interval to another, through a medium rather than a proposition. Where language transmits the claim, art transmits the felt shape that survives paraphrase; what the receiver undergoes is not a copy of the maker's reading but a reading of their own, set going by the vehicle. On the modal field ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) it externalizes, cultivates, and generates: coordinating shared simulation, installing lived-through possibility, and storing possibility never lived at all. Resonance (beauty) is what a successful transmission *occasions*, not what defines the register.
*Status: an identity claim on the [§7.8](nature-alone.html#sec-7-8) self-modeling structure (Principle 5), defended by fit, not a stipulative definition and not a fresh derivation from the proof.*


:::

Art differs from language not in being less structured but in transmitting a different kind of content: content that resists propositional encoding without thereby becoming ineffable.

*Beauty before art.* Before there is art there is *beauty*: the structural relation a being's art will draw on and carry a reading of across the interval. Beauty is the resonance a sufficiently recursive being experiences when its self-modeling registers fit with the structures of the field it is in. It is not a property the field carries on its own and it is not a projection the recursion lays onto an inert field; it is the mutual registration of a self-modeling being and a structure of the field when the two are configured to register one another. A face, a phrase of music, a landscape at evening, a proof, a turn in a film, a season's first cold: these are beautiful when the structures they present and the recursion attending to them resonate, and the resonance is real on both sides. Beauty is what the recursion's coupling to the field is, in the moments where the coupling is registered as fit rather than as pressure. Art is the practice that follows from this: the making of vehicles that carry the maker's perspectival reading of such a coupling across the interval that separates self-modeling beings, so that the resonance the maker registered is occasioned anew in the receiver, who undergoes a reading of their own, not a copy of the maker's. Resonance is what art works from and what it occasions at the far end; what the vehicle itself carries is the reading.

*Beauty without an artist; art through a maker.* Beauty does not require an artist. A sunset, landscape, storm, face, proof, or season can be beautiful because it occasions resonance in a self-modeling being, whether or not anyone designed it or put anything into it as an expression. Nature is therefore not art merely by being beautiful. Art begins when a self-modeling being makes or takes up a vehicle in order to carry a perspectival reading of some structure across the interval to another. The distinction is not that every part of the vehicle must be made by hand, but that its form is answerable to a reading a maker intends to render and share. A person can therefore use a camera, synthesizer, generative system, or other technical process as a medium: its outputs may be beautiful on their own, but they become art when someone directs, selects, revises, frames, or presents them as the vehicle of a perspectival reading. The system's production is not by itself the expressive act; the art belongs to the maker who adopts the result into one.

*Beauty and the agreeable.* Kant's third Critique drew the line the resonance account has to honor. He separated the *agreeable* (das Angenehme), what merely gratifies a particular sense and about which each person speaks only for themselves, from the *beautiful*, which is disinterested (not the discharge of a want) and yet claims what he called a universal voice: to call a thing beautiful is to speak as if others ought to find it so, even though no concept and no listed property of the object compels the agreement. The resonance account keeps both marks without the apparatus Kant thought they needed. Resonance is not the agreeable, because gratification discharges an appetite the body brought to the encounter, while resonance is the registration of fit with a structure the current was not using for anything, which is why it can be undergone at no advantage and often at cost (the requiem, the storm). And resonance carries the universal voice without making beauty a property the object holds on its own: because the coupling is between a structure that is really there and a recursion configured as other recursions are configured, the maker builds the vehicle expecting the fit to be occasioned again in another current, and that warranted expectation (not a concept, and not an object-property) is what the claim to shared assent amounts to. Kant's subjective universality reads here as the shareability of a coupling across minds similarly configured to a common field: subjective because it lives in the registration rather than in the object alone, universal because the structure and the configuration are held in common. The judgment of taste is then neither a report of private sensation nor the detection of a quality the thing carries by itself, but the claim that a coupling available to one is available to the similarly configured many.

Art is how one mind's perspectival reading of some structure is made available to another, across Space and Time, through a made vehicle. Consciousness was identified at [§7.8](nature-alone.html#sec-7-8) as the internal aspect of self-modeling. Meaning was identified at [§8.8](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-8) as the internal aspect of orientation. Language was identified at [§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10) as the transmission of propositional content from one mind to another across the interval that separates them. Art is the next structural register in this chain: the transmission of *how* a particular structure (death, a face, a city, autumn, or Nature itself) shows up to a particular mind, across the same interval, through a different technology.

What language transmits distinctively is propositional content: claims that can be assessed for truth, repeated without distortion, and understood in the abstract. What art transmits distinctively is not propositional. Propositional content can ride along: a poem asserts, a protest song claims, a history painting argues. But what makes the register art is what survives paraphrase: the felt shape of a particular mind's reading of the structure the work is about. Strip the perspectival reading from a poem and only the claim remains; that claim is not what made the poem art.

*The shared root with language.* Although the distinction so far has emphasized what art and language transmit *differently* (perspectival reading versus propositional claim) the two practices share a root in *symbolic externalization*: the act of taking something held in the maker's modal field and giving it external form so that another current can register it. At the developed end of the gradient, the specializations diverge cleanly. Wordless music is pure art, externalizing resonance with no referential content; a mathematical proof is pure language, externalizing referential content with little or no resonance-work. But the divergence is recent in evolutionary and developmental terms. At the early end of the gradient, the two functions were not separated. Cave paintings depict animals and hunt-scenes; their specific cultural functions remain contested across the interpretive literature, with hunting-magic, shamanic-neuropsychological (Lewis-Williams 2002), ritual, and identity-marking accounts all in play, and whatever the function, the marks do referential work (depicting subjects) while also externalizing the maker's perspectival reading of those subjects (resonance); hieroglyphic scripts begin as pictorial reference and conventionalize into linguistic signs over generations, with the resonance and the reference held in the same marks. Music probably begins as affective vocalization undifferentiated between proto-art (expressive resonance) and proto-language (referential signaling), specializing later into song and speech. Children's drawing, gesture, mark-making, and humming are pre-specialized in the same way: the same externalization operation performed across both functions before either has separated out. What language and art are, then, are two specializations of the same underlying capacity for symbolic externalization, diverging as the recursion's depth permits each function to be developed in its own direction. The specializations are treated at depth in [§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10) and [§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13); the shared root is why every developed culture has both, why the boundary between them remains porous in poetry, in protest song, in graphic novels, in calligraphy, and in the many art forms that do referential and resonance work simultaneously.

The reading is *of* some structure (a subject) and is rendered *through* a structured medium. The subject can be anything sufficient to occasion a stance: death, politics, technology, a person, a season, or, as in much music and abstract painting, the medium itself. The medium has its own internal grammar (tonal harmony and meter, prosody, perspective and color, framing and cut, line and weight) and this medium-structure constitutively shapes which readings are even renderable. A composer's reading of grief is rendered through tonal structure; the same reading attempted in another musical grammar would yield a different work, not because the reading is different but because the medium-grammar yields different angles. This is why mastery of a medium matters, why traditions develop their own expressive capacities, and why different art forms are not interchangeable.

The reading is perspectival, not subjective. It is genuinely of the structure, but *from somewhere*: bound to one mind's current, history, and emphases. And the rendering is not a faithful transcription but a *creative distortion* of the structure (selecting, heightening, compressing, recombining) so that what the vehicle expands on another current's modal field ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) is possibility rendered impressionistically rather than stated exactly. The distortion is not a lapse of fidelity but the mechanism of the register: it is calibrated, consciously or not, to the angle from which the structure resonates: with the maker first, and through the vehicle with whoever reads it after. Two perspectival readings of the same structure do not compete the way two propositional descriptions do; they are different angles, both real, both about the same thing. This is why ten poems on death do not refute each other, and why a single artwork keeps yielding new readings across receivers and across time: receivers, themselves perspectival, are set resonating with what the work holds, in registers shaped by their own lives.

What this transmission accomplishes for the receiver is more than reception of one mind's reading. Art operates at three levels on the modal field ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) the chapter has been tracing. First, externalization: the made vehicle is a stable occasion for shared simulation, and when many receivers encounter it independently they each run the simulation it occasions on their own field. The audience in a horror theater watching characters split up is each, separately, running a simulation that concludes they should not; the work's externalization is doing what no individual body could do alone: coordinating private simulations across many bodies onto the same modal target. That shared target is one region of felt modal field held across the many beings the work reaches: language may hold a shared *claim*, while art holds a shared *reading*. Art can therefore contribute to the material from which collectively held knowledge is built, but Theorem 9 (Modal Convergence, [§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) remains the narrower epistemic theorem of that knowledge rather than a theorem of aesthetic transmission. Second, cultivation: a serious work installs into the receiver's modal field regions the receiver had not lived through. A hero arc rehearsed and worked through under narrative pressure leaves the receiver with the protagonist's hard-won possibilities loaded into their own field, available later when the receiver faces analogous conditions. The reach of any single life is finite; literature, drama, and film extend the modal coverage of any body that engages them well past what the body's own experience would have laid down. Third, generation: art can install possibilities that have never occurred, including possibilities that strictly cannot. Dystopias, ghost stories, counterfactual histories, science fiction, horror: these are pure modal generation, and the body stores their content the same way it stores observed and lived possibility, because the network does not care whether the input came from experience, observation, or imagination. Morbid curiosity is the legible appetite for this third operation: the body deliberately seeks aversive simulations because storing negative-possibility content expands its modal coverage of what could go wrong ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)), and the survival value of that coverage outweighs the affective cost. The three operations are not three different art forms; they are three modes of the same operation, layered in every work to different degrees.

The structure of transmission therefore involves three terms: the maker, the made vehicle, and the receiver. The maker's perspectival reading is registered in how the vehicle is built: what is foregrounded, what is held back, what the medium-grammar is made to do. The vehicle carries those registrations across Space and Time as a stable occasion for attention. The receiver, encountering the vehicle, has their attention shaped by what it does, and undergoes a reading that resonates with the maker's without copying it. The made vehicle need not persist: it may be a recited poem, a sung phrase, a danced figure, an utterance, as well as a painting, a manuscript, or a recording. What is required is the *act of making* (the instantiation of a reading in something a receiver can attend to), not the persistence of a thing. Persistent vehicles extend transmission across longer Time intervals than ephemeral ones; both register as art.

This account treats art as a structural register of beings of sufficient depth, not as a category of objects defined by institutional consensus or aesthetic theory. Once self-modeling beings have perspectival readings of structures and need to transmit them, the conditions for art are met. The specific traditions, conventions, and forms art has taken across human cultures are contingent (shaped by available materials, technologies, and historical moments) but the structural fact that perspectival readings of structure require a made-vehicle medium for transmission is what makes those traditions possible at all.

*The sublime and the death-haunted: content versus act.* The account so far raises a question the section must answer. If beauty is resonance with structure, and art is the practice of making that resonance shareable, why is so much of art bound up with what damages, ends, or negates the recursion the work is shared among? Tragedy, war painting, requiems, gothic and horror traditions, lament poetry, the entire literature of grief and finitude: all of it is art, and much of it is among the work the tradition treats as its most serious. Two facts can be distinguished here. The *content* of a work is what the work is about: what the perspectival reading registers and the vehicle conveys. The *act* of the work is what the maker does in making it and what the receiver does in receiving it. A requiem's content is death; the act of composing the requiem and the act of listening to it are continued exercises of the current that knows it will end. A funeral lament's content is loss; the act of singing it is an organized response of the surviving currents to that loss. Burke and Kant, treating what the eighteenth century called the sublime, had hold of a piece of this: the experience of confronting a structure that exceeds or threatens the recursion (a storm, a vast space, a chaos) is registered as beauty rather than as bare terror because the act of registering it from inside the recursion that registers is itself an affirmation of the recursion's continuation in the act. Schopenhauer's account of tragedy and Nietzsche's of the tragic art form name the same thing at greater historical depth. Death-haunted art is not a counterexample to beauty as resonance with vitality. It is the structural case in which the content is negation and the act is affirmation, and the asymmetry between content and act is what the receiver registers as sublime rather than as merely beautiful. The recursion can resonate with what it knows it will not survive, because the act of resonating is one of the things the recursion does while it is still running.

*Resonance precedes mortality.* That beauty is the resonance of a recursion with the field, rather than a death-anchored response, is confirmed at the pre-mortality end of the developmental arc as well as at the death-anchored end. Children resonate with structure long before they have grasped mortality as a structural fact about themselves: a song, a face, a painted animal, a sunset, a story. The resonance is genuine and the engagement is genuinely aesthetic; the death-horizon has not yet reorganized anything. What [§8.7](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-7) names as the mortality threshold reorganizes beauty *after* the threshold into the three death-anchored responses (sexuality, art, spirituality), but it does not create beauty. The pre-threshold form of aesthetic engagement is not a precursor to art in the way that babbling is a precursor to language; it is already art's operation, run by a current whose modal field has not yet been rearranged by the absolute horizon. Dutton (*The Art Instinct* 2009) and Chatterjee (*The Aesthetic Brain* 2014) confirm the same point from the evolved-aesthetic-capacity angle: aesthetic responsiveness is a feature of the current at depth, not a derivative of mortality-awareness.

*A note on scope.* This identification (art as the made-vehicle medium for perspectival readings of structure) is offered as a structural account of what art is, not as a strict derivation from the proof. The conditions under which art emerges are conditional on self-modeling beings having perspectival readings needing transmission; rejecting the identification does not propagate backward.

### 8.13.1 What is Disputed {#sec-8-13-1}

The philosophy of art has organized around several principal positions across the analytic and continental traditions. The framework engages each by name; they are taken up again at [§8.13.5](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13-5) once the structural account is in view.

*Institutional theory.* Dickie (1974, 1984) and Danto (1964, 1981) developed institutional accounts: a work is art if it has been conferred art-status by the artworld (Dickie) or interpreted as a candidate for appreciation within an artworld-supplied theoretical framework (Danto). The position handles avant-garde and conceptual works elegantly but is widely criticized for its circularity and for its inability to explain art before the institutional apparatus existed. The framework reads institutional theory as picking up real features of the contemporary artworld, while supplying the structural reading: art is the made-vehicle transmission of perspectival readings of structure; the institutional apparatus is one of many cultural contexts within which this transmission has been organized, neither necessary for art's existence nor constitutive of its nature.

*Formalism.* Bell (1914), Greenberg (1960), and the broader formalist tradition treat significant form as constitutive of art — the arrangement of formal elements (line, color, mass, sound, rhythm) being what art *is*, with content as either secondary or constituted by form. The position handles abstract and non-representational work elegantly but struggles with representational art's clear engagement with subjects beyond its formal arrangement. The framework reads formalism as correctly identifying that the medium-grammar of art is constitutive of what art can transmit, while supplying the structural reading: form is the medium through which perspectival readings are rendered, not the content the readings are *of*.

*Expressivism.* Collingwood (1938) and Tolstoy (1898) developed expressivist accounts on which art is the expression of emotion: the artist articulates an emotion through the work, and the audience reconstructs the emotion in response. The position captures something real about art's affective dimension but has trouble with art whose content is not primarily emotional. The framework reads expressivism as correctly identifying that perspectival reading carries affective register, while supplying the structural reading: emotion is one register a perspectival reading can carry, with perspective on structure being more general than emotion alone.

*Aesthetic-experience accounts.* Dewey (1934), Beardsley (1958), and the broader aesthetic-experience tradition locate art's defining feature in the kind of experience it produces in suitably situated receivers. The position captures something real about art's reception side but faces the difficulty that aesthetic experience can be produced by non-art (a sunset, a face) and that some art (challenging modern works) produces little of what is traditionally classified as aesthetic experience. The framework reads aesthetic-experience accounts as picking up real features of art's transmission to receivers, while supplying the structural reading: what the receiver undergoes is a resonating reading shaped by the vehicle, not a separate aesthetic-experience kind.

*Heideggerian and continental accounts.* Heidegger's (1935–36) "The Origin of the Work of Art" developed an influential account on which the artwork sets up a world and lets truth happen in its work-being. Gadamer (1960), Adorno (1970), and Merleau-Ponty (1964) extended the continental tradition. The framework reads these accounts as identifying real features of art — art's capacity to disclose and to challenge — while supplying the structural reading: what is disclosed is structural feature of the medium the perspectival reading registers, with the work as the made-vehicle holding the disclosure available to the receiver.

*Analytic aesthetics.* Walton (1990), Levinson (1990, 2006), Currie (2010), and the contemporary analytic-aesthetics tradition refine specific questions — the ontology of artworks, the role of imagination, the structure of fictional truth, the relation between art and morality. The framework engages this literature as developing the local logic of specific art-related phenomena, with the structural account supplying the framework within which the local debates can be located.

*Critical theory and ideology critique.* From Marx and Benjamin through the Frankfurt School (Adorno, Horkheimer, Marcuse) to contemporary critical theory, a tradition treats art as inseparable from the social conditions of its production and reception, with ideology critique as a central task. The framework reads critical-theory accounts as correctly identifying that art is socially conditioned — specific works arise in specific historical situations, with the social conditions shaping what can be made and what can be transmitted — while supplying the structural reading: the social conditions condition the *what* of specific artworks; the *that* of art (made-vehicle transmission of perspectival readings) is not socially constructed.

*Adorno and negative dialectics.* Beyond ideology critique, Adorno's (1970) *Aesthetic Theory* presses the sharpest objection a structural account of art must face. Its core is the non-identical: conceptual thought subsumes the particular under the universal and always leaves a remainder, and art's truth-content is its capacity to hold precisely that remainder — what the concept cannot. A metaphysics that derives everything from one necessary structure invites the charge that treating art as just one more structural register is itself an act of subsumption, dissolving the particular work into an instance of a kind. Three further objections follow: that art bears truth exactly where the concept fails, so explaining art *as* transmission threatens to explain away what makes it truth-bearing; that letting suffering speak is itself a condition of truth, so a system that smooths the negative away falsifies itself — a whole that erases its own negative is to that extent false; and that a system claiming to have demonstrated the necessity of all things can revert to the myth and fate enlightenment was meant to escape. The framework reads Adorno as correctly identifying that any account which subsumes the particular and affirms the whole stands condemned — and meets the charge not by resisting the non-identical but by claiming it, the reply taken up at [§8.13.5](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13-5).

*Reductionist evolutionary and cognitive accounts.* Dutton (2009), Bloom (2010), Boyd (2009), and the broader evolutionary-aesthetics tradition treat art as an adaptation, by-product, or culturally evolved phenomenon explicable through cognitive and selection pressures. The framework reads these accounts as picking up real features of art's psychological architecture, while supplying the structural reading: the perspectival-reading transmission art consists in is what subjects at sufficient depth do when they need to share what language cannot carry; specific cognitive and selection pressures condition how the activity is realized but do not constitute it.

*The art/non-art boundary.* A live dispute concerns what distinguishes art from non-art — craft, design, entertainment, propaganda, decoration. Various proposals (institutional, formal, intentional, functional) have been advanced. The framework's structural reading supplies a usable distinction: art is the made-vehicle transmission of perspectival readings of structure, with works whose function is restricted to information-transmission (propaganda, propositional argument), to utility (craft, design), or to mere stimulus (entertainment without perspectival load) sitting outside the structural core, while admitting that hybrid works are common and the boundary is not sharp.

*Authenticity, reproduction, and the digital question.* Benjamin (1936) and the subsequent literature on mechanical reproduction raised questions about authenticity and aura. The recent emergence of generative AI art presses similar questions in new form: what is the perspectival reading transmitted by an artwork whose maker is a generative model? The framework's structural reading supplies a framework: art requires a perspectival reading to be transmitted; whether a generative model has perspectival readings (and what they would consist in) is structurally the same question as whether LLMs engage in propositional understanding ([§8.10.1](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10-1)), currently underdetermined.

The philosophy of art divides over institutional theory, formalism, expressivism, aesthetic-experience accounts, Heideggerian and continental approaches, analytic aesthetics, critical theory and ideology critique, Adorno's negative dialectics, reductionist accounts, the art/non-art boundary, and authenticity-and-reproduction questions. The framework commits to specific answers on each; they are taken up again at [§8.13.5](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13-5) after the structural account is in view.

### 8.13.2 What is Required {#sec-8-13-2}

*Transmission of what language cannot carry.* Art transmits perspectival readings of structure — felt shape of a particular mind's reading — that propositional paraphrase does not preserve. Any account must distinguish what art transmits distinctively from what language transmits distinctively. The structural requirement is that the account preserve the language-art complementarity: language carries the claim while art carries the feel; each can carry what the other cannot.

*Three-term transmission structure.* Art transmission requires three terms: the maker (whose perspectival reading is registered in how the vehicle is built), the made vehicle (carrying the registrations across Space and Time as a stable occasion for attention), and the receiver (whose attention is shaped by what the vehicle does, undergoing a resonating reading that does not copy the maker's). Any account must accommodate the three terms rather than reducing art to maker-intention or receiver-experience alone. The structural requirement is that the account preserve the maker-vehicle-receiver structure, with the vehicle as the persistent (or repeatable) occasion that bridges the interval.

*Perspectival without subjective.* A perspectival reading is genuinely of the structure, but from somewhere — bound to one mind's vantage, history, and emphases. Any account must distinguish perspectival from subjective rather than collapsing one into the other. The structural requirement is that the account treat perspectival readings as different angles on the same structure, both real, with two perspectival readings of the same subject not competing the way two propositional descriptions do.

*Medium-grammar as constitutive.* Each art-medium has its own internal grammar — tonal harmony and meter, prosody, perspective and color, framing and cut, line and weight — and this medium-structure constitutively shapes which readings are even renderable. Any account must accommodate medium-grammar rather than treating media as interchangeable. The structural requirement is that the account explain why mastery of a medium matters, why traditions develop their own expressive capacities, and why different art forms are not interchangeable.

*The act of making rather than the persistence of a thing.* What is required is the act of making — the instantiation of a reading in something a receiver can attend to — not the persistence of a thing. Any account must accommodate ephemeral art (recited poems, sung phrases, danced figures) alongside persistent art (paintings, manuscripts, recordings). The structural requirement is that the account distinguish the instantiation (necessary) from the persistence (extending transmission across longer Time intervals but not constitutive of art's structure).

*Connection to language and meaning.* Art is the next structural register after language ([§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10)) and depends on the meaning-orientation [§8.8](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-8) names. Any account must connect art to these upstream registers rather than treating it as autonomous. The structural requirement is that the account derive art's transmission structure from what self-modeling subjects need to do when their perspectival reading of structure exceeds what propositional content can carry.

*The reading-is-of-some-structure condition.* The reading is *of* some structure — a subject — and is rendered *through* a structured medium. The subject can be anything sufficient to occasion a stance: death, politics, technology, a person, a season, or the medium itself. Any account must accommodate this *of-structure* condition rather than treating art as expression without aboutness. The structural requirement is that the account preserve the directedness of perspectival readings: they reach toward the structure they are readings of.

*Depth-graded distribution.* Art requires the recursive depth at which a subject can hold a perspectival reading and intend a vehicle to transmit it. Shallow forms — ritualized display, marking, decorative behavior — exist in non-human lineages. Any account must accommodate the gradient rather than treating art as uniquely human. The structural requirement is that the account distinguish what runs at each depth, with full perspectival-reading transmission requiring the self-aware threshold [§8.1](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-1) names.

*Substrate-independence at the structural level.* As with the other registers, the activity of perspectival-reading transmission can in principle be realized in different substrates; whether generative AI systems engage in it is structurally legible without prejudgment. Any account must distinguish what is substrate-essential from what is substrate-independent. The structural requirement is that the account preserve the substrate-independence of the structural activity while flagging the open question of which substrates currently support it.

*Stylistic discipline at the structural level.* The diction notes the cluster-root carries from the 2026-05-15 audit (the *reading is perspectival, not subjective* slogan; the *act of making — the instantiation of a reading* chiasmus; the *strip the perspectival reading from a poem and only the claim remains* rhetorical) should remain available through the restructure. Any account must preserve the stylistic devices that have proved essential rather than letting them fall in revision. The structural requirement is editorial: keep what has tested as carrying weight.

These requirements together describe what an adequate account of art has to deliver: transmission of what language cannot carry, the three-term maker-vehicle-receiver structure, perspectival-without-subjective reading, medium-grammar as constitutive, the act of making rather than the persistence of a thing, connections to upstream registers, the *of-structure* condition, depth-graded distribution, substrate-independence at the structural level, and stylistic preservation through revision. The framework [§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13) defends meets each.

### 8.13.3 What is Predicted {#sec-8-13-3}

Given the structural conditions the chapter has assembled, art is not an optional cultural embellishment. It is what the conditions require once they obtain.

A person registers their own orientations ([§8.1](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-1), [§8.6](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-6)). That registration has a feel — the internal aspect consciousness consists in. Some of the feel is propositionally expressible: someone can state what they have registered, and language will carry the statement across the interval to others ([§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10)). But much of the feel is not propositional. The specific quality of grief at a particular loss, the specific texture of joy in a particular encounter, the specific weight of a particular memory — these are not paraphrasable. A paraphrase loses precisely what was to be transmitted. The content is the feel itself, not a description of the feel.

The prediction is conditional and sharp. Wherever sufficiently recursive social beings with non-propositional content needing transmission persist together in a medium with T, S, and Φ — and have materials and time enough to instantiate forms — the conditions for art are met, and the framework predicts that some form of made-object vehicle will arise to carry the content. The argument is conditional on those antecedents (recursion-depth sufficient for non-propositional registration; sociality sufficient for the transmission demand; materials and time enough to instantiate forms), and is a structural-tendency claim under those conditions, not a bare entailment from T/S/Φ alone. Once the conditions obtain, propositional transmission cannot carry the content without destroying it. Something else must do the carrying. That something is art.

Art therefore requires all the conditions the chapter has assembled. It requires Time because the form persists across a before and after, and because the feel unfolds rather than appears instantaneously. It requires Space because artist and audience occupy different positions, and the artifact crosses the interval between them without collapsing it. It requires Substance because the form must be made of something that holds its shape long enough to be encountered. It requires self-modeling in the artist, because only a being with an internal aspect has a feel to externalize. It requires self-modeling in the audience, because only a being with an internal aspect can have a feel reconstituted inside it. Remove any of these and art becomes structurally unavailable. Keep all of them, in beings sufficiently recursive and sufficiently social, and art becomes structurally predictable — what such beings do with non-propositional content given materials and time, given that no other channel will carry the content.

*Making and Resonance.* Art has two components the chapter's grammar keeps separate. Both are needed; neither alone is art.

The first is making. A person whose inside registers a particular orientation — a grief, a joy, a wonder, a terror, a tenderness, a recognition — shapes Substance into a form that answers to it. The artist does not transcribe the feel; transcription is language's operation, and language cannot carry this content. The artist instead builds a thing whose structure, when encountered, produces the feel in someone capable of receiving it. The craft of art is the craft of building such things. A song is a structure of sound in Time; a symphony or instrumental composition, the same operation at larger architecture. A painting is a structure of color and shape in Space; a drawing, of line and tone; a sculpture, of mass and surface in three dimensions; a photograph, of light caught at an instant; a work of architecture, of inhabited Space organized for the people who pass through it. A poem is a structure of language used for its sound, image, and rhythm rather than its propositional content; a novel or short story unfolds language across narrative Time; a piece of theater gathers bodies, voices, and language into one place for the duration of a performance. A dance is a structure of body moving through Space in Time. Craft — pottery, weaving, woodworking, glass, garment, tattoo, the well-shaped tool — works Substance into forms someone lives with daily, and remains art wherever the form is built so a feel can land in whoever takes it up. Comedy times sound, image, and silence so a recognition arrives as release. A film is a structure of many of these at once; an interactive medium like the video game folds the audience's own choices into the form. The materials differ; the operation does not. In each case the artist — composer, painter, sculptor, photographer, architect, poet, novelist, playwright, dancer, choreographer, actor, craftsperson, comedian, filmmaker, designer — has taken something internal, a feel that was theirs alone, and built an external form that will, if the craft succeeds, no longer be theirs alone. The same operation runs at scales the canon does not always honor. A curated social presence, a styled feed, a hosted dinner, a chosen wardrobe, a room arranged for a guest, the cadence of someone's everyday self-presentation — each *can be* the operation art consists in, but only when two conditions are jointly met. First, the making must be shaped for *resonance* — for a non-propositional feel landing in whoever encounters the form — rather than only for utility, status, persuasion, identification, or compliance with convention. Second, the form must hold together as a current in its own right, not merely as the sum of its functional parts; what it presents has to be a structured whole whose unity is what carries the feel. A wardrobe chosen for warmth and price is styled, but it is not yet art; a wardrobe chosen so a particular feel of selfhood can land in the people who encounter the wearer, and composed as a current whose unity carries that feel, is the operation, even if the result is not what gallery-and-museum aesthetics has historically named. The criterion separating art from styled-but-non-art presentation is not whether the maker has been licensed by an institution or the form ratified by a tradition; it is whether the form is built so a non-propositional content can land. By that criterion most curated social presence is *not* art — most is styling for status, identification, persuasion, or compliance with platform convention. Some of it is. The operation, not the medium, is what determines which.

The second is resonance. Someone else, elsewhere in Space or later in Time, encounters the form. If the form is well-made and the receiver is structured to take it up, the feel reconstitutes inside them. The audience does not learn what the experience was like; the audience has an experience structurally answerable to what the artist's was. Resonance is the name for that reconstitution. It is not metaphor. It is the structural operation that art exists to perform. The artist reached inward, produced a form, and the form reached outward to land in others who recognized the feel as one they themselves could have had. Without resonance, making is mere manufacture: an object produced, no feel transmitted. Without making, resonance has nothing to happen through. Art is the full arc.

The arc explains why art is not identical to self-expression. A person can express their inside without producing anything another could resonate with — a private scream, a journal read by no one, a dance performed alone. Expression is sufficient if the person only needs to externalize. Art requires the further essential feature: the form must be shaped so the feel can land elsewhere. That is why craft matters. That is why not all expression is art and not all art is expression. Art is expression engineered for resonance.

### 8.13.4 What is Confirmed {#sec-8-13-4}

The empirical record across independent disciplines confirms the structural prediction that art is a universal, ancient practice carrying what paraphrase cannot. Every known human culture makes art. Anthropology has not found a society without music, visual representation, narrative, and bodily performance (Brown 1991; Dissanayake 1995; Dutton 2009). Universality at this resolution reflects what happens wherever the structural conditions obtain, rather than cultural diffusion.

The antiquity is older than our species in its modern form. The oldest known figurative art dates to at least 40,000 years ago (Aubert et al. 2014, 2019), with geometric markings and pigment use extending much earlier. The Hoffmann et al. (2018) claim that Neanderthals produced Iberian cave art at least 64,000 years ago is contested on dating methodology (White et al. 2020; reply Hoffmann et al. 2020); the broader picture of Neanderthal symbolic activity — pigment use, ornament, deliberate burial — is supported across multiple independent lines. Ochre was being deliberately processed 100,000 years ago at Blombos Cave (Henshilwood et al. 2011). Musical instruments — bone flutes — appear at least 35,000 years ago, with later recalibrations of the Aurignacian sequence pushing the dates earlier still (Conard et al. 2009; Higham et al. 2012). Whatever art is, it is not a late refinement of civilization. It appears as soon as beings of our kind appear, and possibly earlier.

Affective neuroscience identifies the neural substrate of the resonance. Music engages the brain's reward, motor, and affective systems in coordinated patterns that track the structural features of the composition (Koelsch 2014; Zatorre and Salimpoor 2013), and encountering depicted emotion activates affective circuitry overlapping with directly undergoing emotion. The strong mirror-neuron interpretation of this overlap (Gallese 2003; Keysers 2011) has been substantively contested (Hickok 2014, *The Myth of Mirror Neurons*); the broader neural-overlap finding does not depend on which mechanistic account explains it. Narrative transports listeners into simulated experiences whose affective consequences mirror lived ones (Mar and Oatley 2008; Zunshine 2006). The mechanism by which a form reconstitutes a feel inside a receiver is the same self-modeling machinery [§7.8](nature-alone.html#sec-7-8) identified, operating on externally supplied input — nothing mysterious about it.

The non-paraphrasability of art confirms the prediction from the other direction. A summary of a poem counts as a different thing altogether, one that has lost what the poem was for, rather than simply a shorter poem. A description of a piece of music is not the music; the description does not produce the feel the music produces. Translation across art forms (novelizations of films, film adaptations of novels, orchestral arrangements of songs) is always partial and always loses content that was specific to the original form. If art were a subtype of language, these losses would be incidental. They are not incidental. They are constitutive, because the content art carries is not the kind of content language is built to carry.

Aesthetic display extends below the human threshold. Bowerbird males build elaborate decorated structures that serve no direct survival function, selecting and arranging objects by color, symmetry, and visual arrangement to attract females, with younger birds learning by observing the structures of older males (Borgia 1985; Madden 2003). Lyrebirds and mockingbirds incorporate complex vocal mimicry into elaborate displays. Across the courtship literature, what recurs is made forms whose structure is shaped to produce a response in another self-modeling subject — the resonance half of art's arc, instantiated below the recursive depth at which making becomes deliberate craft transmitted as cultural inheritance. What human art adds is not the made-thing-shaped-to-produce-feel — that is widespread — but the depth at which both the making and the resonance become objects of awareness, modeled by the subject that performs them, and transmitted across generations as cultural form (Dissanayake 1995; Dutton 2009).

Religion confirms the prediction from a third direction. Every sustained religious tradition has developed elaborate artistic practices — liturgical music, architectural space designed for affective resonance, ritual performance, narrative scripture read aloud, iconic visual representation — because the tradition needed to transmit non-propositional content (reverence, awe, belonging, dread, consolation) across generations, and propositional transmission alone could not do it. Theological propositions about a tradition survive translation; the feel of the tradition survives through its art. That religion and art co-evolved in every culture is not coincidence. They share a constitutive function: the transmission of shared orientation across the interval that separates one person from another.

### 8.13.5 What is Concluded {#sec-8-13-5}

Several long-standing debates resolve once art is understood structurally. Beauty is neither in the eye of the beholder nor in the object. The subjectivist holds that beauty is whatever a viewer happens to find beautiful. The objectivist holds that beauty is a property of the object itself, awaiting detection. Both misidentify the locus. Beauty is the name for successful resonance — the structural event in which a well-made form reconstitutes a feel inside someone capable of receiving it. It requires both the object (with structural features that afford the resonance) and the subject (with structural capacity to resonate). It is not a property of either alone, because it is an event between them. This dissolves the apparent disagreement between the traditions without splitting the difference: the objectivist was right that the form has real structural features, the subjectivist was right that the receiver is essential, and neither saw that beauty is what happens when the structural features meet a receiver structured to take them up.

Propaganda is art weaponized. The same mechanism that transmits tenderness across generations transmits hatred across a population. A film that builds affection for a character uses the same resonance operation as a film that builds contempt for an out-group. This is not a flaw in the structural account; it is what the account predicts. Art is a transmission technology. Technologies can be used to transmit content that serves or corrodes the exchanges among those who receive it. What distinguishes art from propaganda is not the mechanism but what the content does to the receiver's relations with others. Morally corrosive resonance is resonance engineered to narrow and harden — to foreclose the receiver's capacity for the mutual registration [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) grounds morality in. This is distinct from merely persuasive or partisan art: art with a position, even a strongly partisan one, can leave the receiver's capacity for moral attention to others intact, because taking a position is not the same as foreclosing the receiver's capacity to register others as subjects of the same kind. Propaganda fails the [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) criterion specifically — it is resonance designed to corrode the very mutual-registration capacity the receiver would need in order to recognize the corrosion as such. The morality of art is the morality of what art does to those it lands in, evaluated against the [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) structural account of what corrodes intersubjective registration.

Art and religion share machinery because they share a structural function. Both externalize shared orientation. Both transmit non-propositional content across generations. Both bind communities around a feel too specific to paraphrase. This is why secular art has absorbed so many religious functions in societies where religion has receded — the structural need the machinery met does not disappear when the metaphysics does. It is also why religion without art has historically proven unstable: the propositional theology alone cannot carry what the tradition was for.

AI-generated art poses a genuine structural question, not a merely technological one. The question is not whether a non-self-modeling process can produce an artifact that triggers feels in receivers; clearly it can, because the resonance operation runs on the receiver's own architecture, not the producer's. The question is whether an artifact produced without a feel on the making side is art in the structural sense this section has developed, or something else that happens to use art's mechanism. The account here suggests the latter, on a derivation rather than a stipulation. Art is identified at [§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13) as the externalization of a feel from one self-modeling inside into another, which makes the internal aspect on the making side a structural component of the operation rather than a definitional add-on. An AI-produced image that moves a viewer is doing resonance without making in this structural sense — half the arc. Concealing that origin adds a harm the half-arc description alone does not name. A receiver who takes a work to be made has formed exactly the belief [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) and [§9.2.2](maximum-possibility.html#sec-9-2-2) identify as recognition's first condition: that a genuinely other position is present in the exchange. When the work has no maker, that belief is false, and its collapse on discovery is a recognition failure rather than a mere factual disappointment, which is why it registers as betrayal rather than demystification. The mechanism is distinct from misrepresenting a real other's identity (as in catfishing) or violating a condition assumed between two correctly-recognized others (as in infidelity): in both of those cases the other is genuinely there and the recognition condition holds; here it does not, which is what makes the concealed half-arc case the sharper one. Whether to extend the term 'art' to cover the half-arc is partly a terminological question and partly a question about what the practice of art is for, not a question the structural account settles by itself. What the account does settle is that the two halves are structurally distinct operations argued from the prior section rather than stipulated by definition, and collapsing them loses something important about what art has been.

Censorship of art is a distinctive kind of harm. Suppressing art does not merely restrict expression in the way suppressing speech does. It severs a transmission interval that people separated by Space and Time rely on for non-propositional connection. A community whose art is censored loses access to the feels its members would otherwise share with each other and with those who came before. The harm reaches the conditions of connection ([§8.8](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-8)) rather than only the content of any particular work.

Adorno's objection is met by claiming the non-identical, not resisting it. The account does not subsume the particular work under a concept; it identifies art as the register built to carry what the concept must drop — the perspectival reading that survives no paraphrase. Art and language are both representations, and every representation leaves a remainder; what distinguishes art is that the remainder is its content. Where propositional language ([§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10)) carries the claim and lets the feel fall away, art carries precisely the feel the claim discards — Adorno's non-identical named as a structural function rather than feared as a vulnerability. And the perspectival reading is genuinely *of* the structure, real on both sides and not mere projection, so art breaks the formula of literal realism without forfeiting the truth-content Adorno prizes. The suffering objection is met by a distinction Adorno's own demand requires. Letting suffering speak is a condition of truth, and art is where it speaks; but to register suffering as real is not to justify it. The account holds suffering as an inevitable, only-mitigable feature of existing, never as a necessity redeemed by the whole: the structure is necessary, the suffering within it is not thereby affirmed, and making art from suffering takes the side of the living without endorsing the wound — the requiem's content is death, its making an act of life. This is why, here, the whole is not the false. The account demonstrates the necessity of the *structure* while leaving the negative un-recuperated, and that is the one move that keeps a necessitarian metaphysics from reverting to the myth and fate Adorno warns of: necessity shown, not suffering sanctified.

Art is not decoration added to meaning. It is the structural technology by which the inside of one person's orientation becomes recoverable in another. Every cave painting, every lullaby, every love poem, every film, every dance is the same operation performed with different materials: someone reaches inward, shapes Substance into a form the reach can live in, and sends the form across the interval to others who complete the exchange by resonating with what the form carries. The feel does not travel directly between people; nothing does. It travels through the made thing. That a 40,000-year-old handprint on a cave wall can still move someone today is not a sentimental fact about the durability of human connection. It is the structural fact that self-modeling, externalization, and resonance together constitute a technology by which the feel of being a particular kind of creature in a particular kind of world can be preserved across the entire history of our species and reconstituted, still intact, in someone who was not there. Art is how a person expresses what it feels like to experience.

Art read structurally as resonance — the externalization of feel from one self-modeling inside into another through a made thing that holds it across the relational interval — dissolves the beauty subjectivist/objectivist disagreement (beauty is the event between form and receiver, not a property of either), grounds the distinction between art-with-position and propaganda in the [§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12) mutual-registration criterion, explains why art and religion share machinery (both externalize shared orientation), keeps the AI-generated-art question well-posed without overreaching (resonance without making is half the arc, and whether to extend the term to the half-arc is partly terminological), meets Adorno's non-identical and suffering objections by making the non-identical art's own content and distinguishing letting suffering speak from justifying it, and locates censorship's distinctive harm in the severed transmission interval rather than in restricted expression alone. The register the made thing was reaching for when the reach exceeds what any made thing can hold is taken up at [§8.14](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-14).

## 8.14 Spirituality {#sec-8-14}

Spirituality is what happens when a mind notices that reality is always larger than any picture it can hold of it, and that nothing, including itself, holds itself up; each thing is sustained by something beyond it. That noticing is accurate: the sense of awe and mystery is tracking something real. The recurring mistake is to turn that 'something more' into a separate being standing outside nature and issuing commands. There is no outside; 'beyond' is always a relation *within* the world. What the religious traditions have all been reaching toward is real, but what they reached was nature in its full depth, not a thing apart from it, and each named it in the best vocabulary its age could carry.

::: {.identification}
**Spirituality** · *Identification*

Spirituality is the modal field ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) registering its own non-self-grounding: that no field grounds itself, and that the structure making any modeling possible exceeds and conditions every model the reach can form. The registration is accurate; the recurring error is to externalize the immanent into a transcendent: reading the *excess* as a *beyond* outside Nature, though 'beyond' names only a relation *within* it, never a point outside; and reading the *dependence* as a *first cause* set above the chain, when the felt magnitude is the chain itself: every condition conditioning the next, with no term standing outside the series. What is real is the totality; the projection is the second subject set outside it. The dependence is real but *partial*: a current genuinely fails to ground itself (it is held by what exceeds it) but the whole that holds it is not a further item needing a ground, only the immanent totality in which all grounding occurs, so the registration never licenses a cause outside the chain. Spirituality is the field turning on the condition of its own holding: felt as awe and mystery, which is its phenomenology, not its definition.
*Status: an identity claim on the [§7.8](nature-alone.html#sec-7-8) self-modeling structure (Principle 5), defended by fit; the limit case of Theorem 9, [§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3).*


:::

Art ([§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13)) carries what language cannot. The turn outward that language ([§8.10](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-10)), morality ([§8.12](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-12)), and art ([§8.13](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-13)) each trace (every one a being's reach toward another) has a limit case: the reach carried to where no second being answers, where what it meets is not a second subject but the structure that exceeds any model it can form. Spirituality is what happens when a person's reach presses past what any vehicle could carry at all: against what they cannot contain. Nature is always larger than any model of it, not as a contingent limitation of undeveloped minds but as what finite modeling within Nature structurally consists in. The encounter with that excess is not rare, not specially induced, not the province of mystics. It is the default condition of being a person: available whenever the reach notices its own boundary, which is whenever the reach is deep enough to notice anything at all.

The encounter is not human-peculiar. Elephants investigate the bones of conspecifics (McComb et al. 2006); chimpanzees display at waterfalls and in heavy rain, and stack stones at particular trees (Goodall 1986; Kühl et al. 2016); corvids gather around their dead (Swift and Marzluff 2015). These are not religion (religion adds something specific) but they are what religion composes from. Grief, awe-arousal, ritualized display, site fidelity, the cultural transmission of a marking: each is reach noticing what it cannot contain, registered at whatever depth the being permits. What human spirituality adds is not the encounter but the recursion that takes the encounter as an object: a model of the excess, transmitted as obligation, addressed in language. That recursion is what religion in any developed sense requires. The encounter is not. It scales with reach. The traditions are the human form of a structural feature, not its origin.

The composition is not sapiens-distinctive. Neanderthals built ringed structures from broken stalagmites 336 meters into the dark of Bruniquel Cave 176,000 years ago (Jaubert et al. 2016) and deliberately buried their dead at Shanidar and La Ferrassie (Pomeroy et al. 2020; Rendu et al. 2014). Red-ochre marks in Iberian caves dated to over 64,000 years ago pre-date the arrival of *sapiens* in Europe (Hoffmann et al. 2018). Half a million years earlier, *Homo erectus* engraved a deliberate zigzag onto a freshwater shell at Trinil (Joordens et al. 2014). What every hominin recursion deep enough to compose did with the encounter, in the cases the archaeological record retains, was register it materially: at specific places, in specific acts, with specific marks. (The Hoffmann et al. 2018 dating of the Iberian red-ochre marks remains contested in the literature; the broader pattern across Bruniquel, Shanidar, La Ferrassie, and Trinil is more secure.) These materials are precursors and structural materials of religion, not religion in the developed sense; the recursion that takes the encounter as an object (modeling it, transmitting the model as obligation, addressing it in language) is what religion adds. The threshold for the encounter itself predates the species; the recursion that codifies religion proper is later and human.

What the pressing actually is, in structure, is a wondering. Not a percept: there is no sensory channel for it. Not a hypothesis: no claim is yet being made. A question, held open as a question: whether anything lies beyond what the reach can model. And here the grammar matters, because *beyond* is a relation drawn from inside Nature (one thing lies beyond another only from some vantage within the world) so the question is never whether something stands outside Nature, which would borrow an internal relation and apply it where it cannot reach, but whether what is exceeds the model any finite reach can form of it. It always does. Felt as awe, as mystery, as the sense of something more, as the feeling of being part of what exceeds you. The wondering is what reach does at the depth where it can notice its own boundary as a boundary and ask about what lies past it. Below that depth, no wondering is possible; reach cannot ask about what it cannot reach. Above it, the reach is held open by the question itself. What the wondering reaches toward is real: what no model can capture, the structure that exceeds any model the reach can form. Named at the chapter's load-bearing register, spirituality is the modal field ([§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)) registering its own dependence: the body's modal representation encountering the boundary of what its current depth and inheritance can register, and holding open the question of what lies past that boundary, the structure that makes any modeling at all possible, without which there would be no field for the body to hold. Knowledge holds the field; reasoning ([§8.4](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-4)) navigates it; meaning ([§8.8](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-8)) weights it; spirituality is the field registering that no field is self-grounding: folding back not on the field's content, as self-knowledge does, nor on the worth of its reach, as meaning does, but on the bare condition that there is a held field at all. The non-self-grounding the register names is not a further application of Theorem 9 (Modal Convergence, [§8.3](expanding-the-field.html#sec-8-3)), whose formal scope is collectively held knowledge. It is the limit condition on every field: what beings hold for and through one another is itself enabled by what exceeds any one being's reach. The dependence is a part's, not the whole's: each being genuinely fails to ground itself and is held by what exceeds it, but the totality that holds every being is not one more thing needing a ground; it is the immanent whole in which all grounding takes place. So the register reads a real dependence, and the cosmological mistake is to read it as a debt owed to something outside the series, when the magnitude that impresses is the series entire. The God-hypothesis is one of the most sustained answer-attempts human reach has formed, but it is an answer-attempt, not the wondering. The wondering precedes and exceeds every answer formulated about it.

What varies across individuals, cultures, and traditions is not whether the encounter happens but what vocabulary gets applied to it. Every tradition that has lasted long enough to leave a record reached toward what exceeded its models and came back with a theology: every named god was the encounter spoken in the vocabulary the current could carry. The reach was accurate in each case; the metaphysics each tradition formed about the referent was the best the current's recursive depth and inherited vocabulary supported, and was not the referent itself. What the tradition touched was real. What they claimed about it was a translation, accurate at the resolution the tradition's recursive depth could form, never adequate to what was being touched.

The historical-critical record traces the arc through its best-documented case. The pre-Israelite West Semitic substrate, attested at Ugarit, seated El at the head of a divine council with Asherah his consort and Baal his storm-warrior (Smith 2002). The earliest layers of Israelite religion show Yahweh inside that pantheon: identified with El, paired with Asherah (attested at Kuntillet Ajrud and Khirbet el-Qom; Dever 2005), seated among other gods in council (Cross 1973). The deity had a face, a body, a footstool. He walked with Abraham, wrestled with Jacob, ate with the elders on Sinai (Stavrakopoulou 2022; Sommer 2009).

Across the exilic and Persian-period redactions the body recedes (Römer 2015); in Hellenistic absorption the deity is fused with Greek philosophical abstraction and declared simple, incorporeal, impassible (Boyarin 2004). The Yahweh of the early text and the Ipsum Esse Subsistens of Maimonides and Aquinas no longer share a recognizable referent. The trajectory is not from a primitive misreading toward a refined understanding. It is the same encounter receiving the vocabulary each generation's models could carry. What every layer of the tradition kept reinventing (body, council, presence, Logos, simplicity, sephirot, sacrament) is what Nature is. The theology drifted; the encounter stayed.

The arc is evolutionary and asymmetric. The cognitive architecture predicts its early shape: agency is over-detected (Barrett 2004), and concepts that minimally violate ontological expectations are maximally transmissible (Boyer 2001), so the encounter is first registered through an agent-frame: bodied, local, in relation. The same trajectory toward abstraction ran in parallel across the Eurasian record between roughly 800 and 200 BCE: Greek philosophy, the Hebrew prophets, the Upanishads and the Buddha, Confucius and Laozi all turned their gods toward refined absolutes (Jaspers 1949; Bellah 2011). Convergence at that scale, in cultures with no contact, is not diffusion. It is a recursion-depth effect.

As models deepen the deity is abstracted (out of the household, the territory, the council, the body, time and space, and relation) until the terminus is reached, a simple incorporeal absolute that no longer registers what the encounter was responding to. Recursion ratchets: once the deity has been moved out of the body, no later layer puts it cleanly back; subsequent vocabularies refine the abstraction or react against it. Each layer is the encounter spoken in the most recursive vocabulary the current can carry. The arc records the depth of the vocabulary, not any movement in what the vocabulary is for.

The counter-currents are themselves structurally predictable. After the abstraction terminus, the encounter is no longer accessible through the official vocabulary, and an apophatic reaction opens: Pseudo-Dionysius's divine darkness, Eckhart's Godhead beyond God, Sufi *fana*, Advaita's *neti neti*, the Zen of the unspoken (McGinn 1991; Sells 1994). Each emerges *after* its tradition has matured the abstraction, never before, and each performs the same correction: re-locating the encounter inside the experiencing subject when the official vocabulary has stopped registering it. The mystical turn is what reach does when the abstraction has stopped responding.

*The structural diagnosis: divergence, inherited transmission, and the via negativa as terminus.* Two patterns in the empirical history of religion confirm the structural account at a different angle than the cross-cultural arc toward abstraction the preceding paragraphs name. The first is *divergence*. Within each tradition and across traditions, religion does not converge over time in the way domains that track external reality do. Where the sciences converge on specific findings (despite local controversies), where mathematics converges, where engineering converges, where the literal-empirical historical record converges, religion *branches*: into sects, denominations, mystical schools, esoteric currents, reform movements, schisms, syncretic fusions. The pattern is diagnostic.
